label: Mixpanel
description: Arcade.dev LLM tools for Mixpanel product analytics

tools.name: AggregateProperty
tools.description:
Sum or average a numeric event property over time.

Use this for value metrics -- revenue, order size, duration -- where the answer
is a total or a mean rather than a count of events.

Aggregates one event at a time, so a project-wide total needs one call per
event carrying the property.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Exact name of the event carrying the property, matching how the event is tracked in Mixpanel. Mixpanel aggregates one event at a time.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: Numeric property to aggregate. A bare property name is wrapped automatically; a full arithmetic expression over properties["NAME"] terms is also accepted.

parameters.name: aggregation
parameters.description: How to combine the values. Defaults to 'sum'.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Start of the window. Accepts an absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD), an offset (-Nd, -Nw, -Nm, -Ny), or a named range (last N days/weeks/months, this or last week/month/quarter/year, month to date, year to date, today, yesterday). An offset here opens a window of that length ending at to_date, so -7d with to_date 'today' is the seven days ending today; as an end bound the same offset names that day itself. A named range sets both ends of the window and to_date is ignored. Defaults to 'last 30 days'.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: End of the window, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'yesterday', or an offset back from today such as -1d or -2w, which names that day itself). Ignored when the start names a whole range. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Bucket size. Defaults to 'day'.

output.description: The aggregated value with its per-bucket points and the date window that was queried.

tools.name: ComparePeriods
tools.description:
Compare one event's volume between two periods, matched in length.

Reports the absolute change, the percentage change, and the direction, so the
"is this up or down" question is answered directly rather than left as
arithmetic over two payloads. A comparison window given explicitly can end up
shorter when it runs into today, and notes says so when it does.

This is also how to get one whole-window figure for unique_users or
average_events_per_user: each window is measured as a single span rather
than per bucket. It takes no breakdown, so it cannot answer a per-segment
question, and it fails rather than answering if Mixpanel does not reduce a
window to one figure.

Costs two of the 60 Mixpanel queries available per hour.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Exact event name, matching how the event is tracked in Mixpanel.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Start of the current window. Accepts an absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD), an offset (-Nd, -Nw, -Nm, -Ny), or a named range (last N days/weeks/months, this or last week/month/quarter/year, month to date, year to date, today, yesterday). An offset here opens a window of that length ending at to_date, so -7d with to_date 'today' is the seven days ending today; as an end bound the same offset names that day itself. A named range sets both ends of the window and to_date is ignored. Defaults to 'last 7 days'.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: End of the window, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'yesterday', or an offset back from today such as -1d or -2w, which names that day itself). Ignored when the start names a whole range. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: compare_from_date
parameters.description: First day of the comparison window (YYYY-MM-DD, 'yesterday', or an offset back from today such as -60d, which names that day itself). The window runs forward from it for as long as the current one, clipped at today. Defaults to the period immediately before the current window, which is almost always what is wanted.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Bucket size for both series. Applies to total_events only; unique_users and average_events_per_user are measured over each window as a whole and ignore this. Defaults to 'day'.

parameters.name: count_type
parameters.description: How occurrences are counted. Defaults to 'total_events'.

parameters.name: filter_expression
parameters.description: Only count events, in both windows, that match this Mixpanel filter expression over event properties. Write it in the form properties["NAME"] OPERATOR VALUE. Supports ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in, and/or/not, and defined(properties["NAME"]). Defaults to no filtering.

output.description: Both windows' totals with the absolute change, percentage change and direction, plus each window's series.

tools.name: GetEngagementFrequency
tools.description:
Get how habitually users perform an event.

Buckets users by how many distinct periods they were active in, separating
one-time users from a habitual core. Answers how sticky a feature is, which a
plain event count cannot. Buckets are cumulative thresholds, so they overlap
and do not sum to the user base.

Mixpanel measures each unit cohort separately and cannot dedupe users across
them, so total_users is a distinct headcount only when the window resolves to
one cohort and is null otherwise -- which the defaults produce, since a
30-day window holds four or five weekly cohorts. Quote peak_users_per_cohort
for scale, or query a window of one unit for a distinct total.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Exact event name, matching how the event is tracked in Mixpanel.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Start of the window. Accepts an absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD), an offset (-Nd, -Nw, -Nm, -Ny), or a named range (last N days/weeks/months, this or last week/month/quarter/year, month to date, year to date, today, yesterday). An offset here opens a window of that length ending at to_date, so -7d with to_date 'today' is the seven days ending today; as an end bound the same offset names that day itself. A named range sets both ends of the window and to_date is ignored. Defaults to 'last 30 days'.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: End of the window, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'yesterday', or an offset back from today such as -1d or -2w, which names that day itself). Ignored when the start names a whole range. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Length of each analysis cohort. Defaults to 'week'.

parameters.name: activity_period
parameters.description: The period a user is counted as active in. Defaults to 'day'.

parameters.name: filter_expression
parameters.description: Only count events that match this Mixpanel filter expression over event properties. Write it in the form properties["NAME"] OPERATOR VALUE. Supports ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in, and/or/not, and defined(properties["NAME"]). Defaults to no filtering.

output.description: Cumulative buckets of users by how many periods they were active in, each with its share of the active user base.

tools.name: GetEventTrend
tools.description:
Get a time series for one event, optionally split by a property.

A window-wide total comes back for total_events. Unique users and per-user
averages are counted within each bucket, so they report no window total
unless the window resolves to a single bucket.

Splitting by a property answers "which segment drove this" in one query.
Mixpanel allows only 60 queries per hour, so a single split query is
substantially cheaper than one filtered query per segment.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Exact event name, matching how the event is tracked in Mixpanel.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Start of the window. Accepts an absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD), an offset (-Nd, -Nw, -Nm, -Ny), or a named range (last N days/weeks/months, this or last week/month/quarter/year, month to date, year to date, today, yesterday). An offset here opens a window of that length ending at to_date, so -7d with to_date 'today' is the seven days ending today; as an end bound the same offset names that day itself. A named range sets both ends of the window and to_date is ignored. Defaults to 'last 30 days'.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: End of the window, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'yesterday', or an offset back from today such as -1d or -2w, which names that day itself). Ignored when the start names a whole range. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Bucket size for the time series. Defaults to 'day'.

parameters.name: count_type
parameters.description: How occurrences are counted. Only total_events adds up across buckets and segments, so it is the only one that reports a window-wide grand_total; for the other two grand_total is null unless the window resolves to a single bucket. Defaults to 'total_events'.

parameters.name: segment_by_property
parameters.description: Property name to split the series by, giving one series per value. Defaults to a single combined series.

parameters.name: filter_expression
parameters.description: Only count events that match this Mixpanel filter expression over event properties. Write it in the form properties["NAME"] OPERATOR VALUE. Supports ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in, and/or/not, and defined(properties["NAME"]). Defaults to no filtering.

parameters.name: segment_limit
parameters.description: Maximum segments to request when splitting by a property (1-1000). Defaults to 50.

output.description: One series per segment, each with its per-bucket points, total, peak and first-to-last change, plus the date window that was queried.

tools.name: GetFunnel
tools.description:
Get step-by-step conversion for a saved Mixpanel funnel.

Takes the funnel's name or its numeric ID and resolves a name against the
project's saved funnels, so there is no need to list them first.

Steps are aggregated across the whole window rather than split into per-date
sub-funnels.

Costs two of the 60 Mixpanel queries available per hour.

parameters.name: funnel
parameters.description: The saved funnel to query, given either as its name or its numeric ID. Names are resolved against the project's saved funnels, and a unique partial name is accepted.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Start of the window. Accepts an absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD), an offset (-Nd, -Nw, -Nm, -Ny), or a named range (last N days/weeks/months, this or last week/month/quarter/year, month to date, year to date, today, yesterday). An offset here opens a window of that length ending at to_date, so -7d with to_date 'today' is the seven days ending today; as an end bound the same offset names that day itself. A named range sets both ends of the window and to_date is ignored. Defaults to 'last 30 days'.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: End of the window, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'yesterday', or an offset back from today such as -1d or -2w, which names that day itself). Ignored when the start names a whole range. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: conversion_window_days
parameters.description: Days a user has to finish the funnel after entering it (1-90). Defaults to the conversion window saved with the funnel in Mixpanel.

output.description: Each funnel step with its count, step and overall conversion and average timings, plus the largest drop-off.

tools.name: GetRetention
tools.description:
Get a cohort retention table with retention percentages computed.

The size-weighted average curve across cohorts is the figure usually meant by
"our day-7 retention".

Intervals are indexed as Mixpanel buckets them: index 0 holds users who came
back within the first period and runs close to 100%, and index N is retention
N periods out. first_time retention reports a window-wide headcount in
total_cohort_size; recurring re-enrols a user in every period they act in, so
the cohorts overlap and that field comes back null.

parameters.name: born_event
parameters.description: Exact name of the event that starts the cohort clock, such as a signup or activation event.

parameters.name: return_event
parameters.description: Exact name of the event that counts as returning. Defaults to an empty string, which reuses born_event to measure whether users repeat it.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Start of the cohort window. Accepts an absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD), an offset (-Nd, -Nw, -Nm, -Ny), or a named range (last N days/weeks/months, this or last week/month/quarter/year, month to date, year to date, today, yesterday). An offset here opens a window of that length ending at to_date, so -7d with to_date 'today' is the seven days ending today; as an end bound the same offset names that day itself. A named range sets both ends of the window and to_date is ignored. Defaults to 'last 8 weeks'.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: End of the window, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'yesterday', or an offset back from today such as -1d or -2w, which names that day itself). Ignored when the start names a whole range. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Length of each retention interval. Defaults to 'day'.

parameters.name: retention_kind
parameters.description: Which retention question to ask. Defaults to 'first_time'.

parameters.name: intervals
parameters.description: Number of retention intervals to return (1-90). Defaults to 14.

parameters.name: filter_expression
parameters.description: Only count return events that match this Mixpanel filter expression over event properties. Write it in the form properties["NAME"] OPERATOR VALUE. Supports ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in, and/or/not, and defined(properties["NAME"]). Defaults to no filtering.

output.description: One row per cohort with its size, per-interval counts and retention percentages, plus the size-weighted average curve across cohorts.

tools.name: GetSavedReport
tools.description:
Read the data behind a saved Mixpanel Insights report.

This is Mixpanel's supported way to query a report whose definition already
lives in the product, including breakdown and funnel report types that have no
direct API of their own.

The report's own saved date range and filters apply and cannot be overridden
through the API. Nested breakdowns are flattened to one series per segment.

parameters.name: report_id
parameters.description: Numeric ID of the saved Insights report. It appears in the report's URL as the digits in the editor card reference, formatted report-<ID>.

output.description: The report's series with totals, the date range saved with the report, and when Mixpanel computed the figures.

tools.name: GetUserActivity
tools.description:
Get one user's chronological event history, newest first.

Use this to trace an individual journey -- reproducing a support report, or
seeing what a user did before churning.

parameters.name: distinct_id
parameters.description: The user's Mixpanel distinct_id, the unique profile identifier.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Start of the window. Accepts an absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD), an offset (-Nd, -Nw, -Nm, -Ny), or a named range (last N days/weeks/months, this or last week/month/quarter/year, month to date, year to date, today, yesterday). An offset here opens a window of that length ending at to_date, so -7d with to_date 'today' is the seven days ending today; as an end bound the same offset names that day itself. A named range sets both ends of the window and to_date is ignored. Defaults to 'last 7 days'.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: End of the window, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'yesterday', or an offset back from today such as -1d or -2w, which names that day itself). Ignored when the start names a whole range. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum events to return (1-200). Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0 (most recent event).

output.description: A page of the user's events, newest first, with timestamps and properties.

tools.name: ListCohorts
tools.description:
List the saved cohorts in this Mixpanel project, largest first.

Cohorts are created in the Mixpanel UI; they cannot be created here.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum cohorts to return (1-200). Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0 (first result).

output.description: A page of saved cohorts with their names, IDs and last computed member counts.

tools.name: ListEventProperties
tools.description:
List the property names recorded on an event, most frequent first.

These names are the valid inputs for segmenting or filtering this event in the
analytics tools.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Exact event name, matching how the event is tracked in Mixpanel.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum properties to return (1-200). Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0 (first result).

output.description: A page of property names recorded on the event, with how often each one appears.

tools.name: ListEvents
tools.description:
List the event names tracked in this Mixpanel project, ranked by volume.

Event names must be given to analytics tools exactly as tracked -- they are
case- and punctuation-sensitive, so "Sign Up" and "sign_up" are different
events. Returns the highest-volume events first.

parameters.name: ranking_window
parameters.description: Window to rank event volume over. 'today' also reports each event's percent change against yesterday. Defaults to 'last_31_days'.

parameters.name: count_type
parameters.description: How occurrences are counted. Defaults to 'total_events'.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum events to return (1-200). Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0 (first result).

output.description: A page of tracked event names ranked by volume, with pagination fields.

tools.name: ListFunnels
tools.description:
List the saved funnels in this Mixpanel project, with their IDs.

Mixpanel can only report on funnels that were saved in its UI; there is no way
to define an ad-hoc funnel over arbitrary events through the API.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum funnels to return (1-200). Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0 (first result).

output.description: A page of saved funnels with their names and numeric IDs.

tools.name: ListProfiles
tools.description:
Find Mixpanel user profiles by property filter or cohort membership.

A cohort is given by name or numeric ID and a name is resolved here, so there
is no need to list cohorts first.

Pages hold up to 1000 profiles; to read further ones, pass back the returned
session_id with an incremented page number.

Profile properties are a separate namespace from event properties; a filter
written against an event property will not match anything here.

parameters.name: match_mode
parameters.description: Whether to select profiles by a property filter or by membership of a saved cohort. Defaults to 'filter'.

parameters.name: filter_expression
parameters.description: Only return profiles that match this Mixpanel filter expression over *profile* properties. Used only when selecting by filter. Write it in the form properties["NAME"] OPERATOR VALUE. Supports ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in, and/or/not, and defined(properties["NAME"]). Defaults to all profiles.

parameters.name: cohort
parameters.description: The saved cohort whose members to return, given as its name or numeric ID. Required when match_mode is 'cohort', ignored otherwise. Defaults to no cohort.

parameters.name: output_properties
parameters.description: Exact profile property names to return. A long explicit list makes responses substantially larger and slower. Defaults to a compact identity set covering email, name, creation and last-seen dates, and location.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 0-indexed page number. Mixpanel pages profiles in fixed blocks of 1000 rather than by arbitrary offset. Defaults to 0 (first page).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The session_id returned by a previous call. Required for any page after the first, and makes paging much faster by reusing Mixpanel's cached result set. Defaults to a new result set, which only works for page 0.

output.description: A page of matching profiles with the requested properties, and the session_id needed to request further pages.

tools.name: ListPropertyValues
tools.description:
List the values observed for one property of an event.

Use this to get filter values exactly right: a filter on a value that does not
exist returns zero rows, which is indistinguishable from a genuine absence of
activity.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Exact event name, matching how the event is tracked in Mixpanel.

parameters.name: property_name
parameters.description: Exact property name as recorded on that event.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum values to return (1-200). Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0 (first result).

output.description: A page of values observed for the property.

tools.name: WhoAmI
tools.description:
Verify the Mixpanel connection and list the projects it can reach.

Confirms the service account authenticates, reports the configured region and
project, and checks that the configured project is one the service account can
actually read -- the usual cause of empty results or permission errors.

output.description: The authenticated service account, the region and project in use, and the organizations and projects that account can reach.

summary:
Mixpanel is a product analytics platform. This toolkit lets agents query a Mixpanel project's events, funnels, retention, cohorts, user profiles, and saved reports with a service account.

## Capabilities

- **Event trends and totals**: get an event's time series, optionally split by a property; sum or average a numeric property; and compare an event's volume between two periods of equal length.
- **Funnels, retention, and engagement**: read conversion for a saved funnel, cohort retention tables, and how habitually users repeat an event.
- **Saved reports**: read the data behind a saved Insights report, including breakdown and funnel reports.
- **Users**: find user profiles by property or cohort, and read one user's event history.
- **Discovery**: list events, event properties, property values, saved funnels, and cohorts, so filters use exact names and values.
- **Connection check**: confirm the service account authenticates and can read the configured project and region.

Mixpanel allows 60 queries per hour, and funnel and period comparisons each use two.

## Secrets

- `MIXPANEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_USERNAME`: the username of a Mixpanel service account. Create the service account in your Mixpanel organization settings and give it access to the project you want to query. See [Mixpanel service accounts](https://developer.mixpanel.com/reference/service-accounts).
- `MIXPANEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET`: the service account's secret. Mixpanel shows it only once, when you create the service account, so save it then.
- `MIXPANEL_PROJECT_ID`: the numeric ID of the project to query. Find it in the project's settings in Mixpanel, or run `Mixpanel.WhoAmI` to list the projects the service account can reach.
- `MIXPANEL_REGION`: the data residency region of the project, such as `US` or `EU`. It decides which Mixpanel API host the tools call, so a wrong value causes authentication errors or empty results. Check the project's data residency in its Mixpanel settings.

Store the secrets in Arcade as described in the [Arcade secrets docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets), or manage them in the [Arcade dashboard](https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets).
